# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 8
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 8

---

*[THE EUCHARIST. Bread and water. No wine. An ancient prayer. Mygdonia arrives.]*

1. After the baptisms, Thomas broke bread. He gave thanks over it and prayed aloud — a prayer like nothing else in early Christian literature:

   "Come, O holy name of Christ that is above every name.
   Come, power of the Most High and perfect mercy.
   Come, thou highest gift.
   Come, compassionate mother.
   Come, thou that knowest the mysteries of the Chosen One.
   Come, thou who art present in all the movements of the Chosen One.
   Come, Holy Spirit — purify their hearts, and seal them
   in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit."

2. Then he broke the eucharist and gave a portion to each person. "Let this eucharist be for you," he said — "life, forgiveness of sins, and eternal resurrection."

3. "Amen," they said.

4. There was a woman there named Mygdonia — wife of Charisius, a relative of the king. She saw Thomas and felt herself drawn to him powerfully, irresistibly.

5. She pushed through the crowd until she was standing beside him.

6. Thomas looked at her. "Who are you?" he said. "What do you want?"

7. "I am Mygdonia," she said. "I want to hear the word of life from you."

8. Thomas looked at her with joy. "Blessed are you, Mygdonia," he said. "You have sought the one thing necessary. I will give you the living water that satisfies all thirst, and the bread of heaven that satisfies all hunger."

9. He gave her the eucharist, and she took it with joy in her hands.

10. That night, Thomas took oil and poured it over his own head. Then he prayed again — a longer, stranger prayer:

    "Come, holy name of Christ.
    Come, power of the Most High.
    Come, gift of the Most High.
    Come, compassionate father.
    Come, fellowship of the male.
    Come, revealer of hidden mysteries.
    Come, mother of the seven houses,
       whose rest was in the eighth house.
    Come, elder of the five members —
       intelligence, thought, prudence, reflection, reasoning —
       communicate with these young men."

11. After the anointing, he laid his hands over those present and prayed: "Let the mercy of the Holy Spirit come and rest upon them."

---
*PNEUMA note: The two prayers in this chapter (vv.1 and 10) are among the oldest Eucharistic and anointing prayers in any Christian text. The Holy Spirit is addressed as "compassionate mother" — the Syriac Spirit (*Ruha*) is grammatically feminine, and early Syriac Christianity developed rich maternal Spirit-theology. The oil prayer's reference to "seven houses / eighth house" is cosmological — seven heavens and the transcendent eighth — the goal of the soul's ascent. Rendered in verse form to honor the liturgical register.*
